items.Name: The Great War and Twin Cataclysms
items.Description:
Just over one thousand years ago, two ancient western empires, the Suel and the Baklunish, were enmeshed in titanic conflict. The root of animosity between them is lost, but the result of their final war haunts even the modern historian.  

After sixty-three years of conflict, t…

items.Name: Suloise Folklore
items.Description: When the Rain of Colorless Fire ended the Age of Glory and brought down the Empire, the tribes decided to seek their fate to the east, in the lands of the Flan. To expidite this migration, Slerotin, the Last Mage of Power, caused a great tunnel to be magically made through the n…

items.Name: The Great Migrations
items.Description: Thousands survived the Twin Cataclysms by fleeing east over the Crystalmists in the early years of the conflict. The Oeridians, a confederation of tribes nestled between the empires, took the wars as a sign from their gods to continue migrating far to the east. They were the fir…

items.Name: City of Greyhawk
items.Description:
People of all nations and races can be found in this thriving metropolis, and trade from all across the Flanaess passes through Greyhawk.  

The people of Greyhawk pursue knowledge and wealth. The University of Magical Arts and the Grey College, among its many schools, attract s…

items.Name: Founding of Keoland
items.Description: The most successful union of Suel and Oerid was the Kingdom of Keoland, founded some eighty years after the Twin Cataclysms. Suel Houses joined with Oeridian tribes on the banks of the Sheldomar River and pledged themselves to mutual protection and dominian of the western Flanae…

items.Name: Wild Coast
items.Description: The western shores of the Sea of Gearnat have long been called the Wild Coast, for the region has been a haven for malcontents, dissidents, demi-humans, humanoids, and the outcasts of other states. It is a fair but not particularly fertile area - rolling countryside interspersed…

items.Name: Bodies of Water: Azure Sea
items.Description: Trading here is age-old, despite local pirates and sea monsters. This body of water is one of the main carriers of commerce between west and central nations. Free-booters are fairly common, and the savages inhabiting the islands of the Amedio coast practice piracy. There are a s…

items.Name: Bodies of Water: Gearnat, Sea of
items.Description: The Sea of Gearnat is a long, curved bay whose ends have separate names: Woolly Bay on the west, and Relmor Bay on the east. Superb navigational charts exist for the whole area. The Gearnat was once known as the Sea of Yar, after a famed Suel explorer who proved to be an enemy o…

items.Name: Bodies of Water: Woolly Bay
items.Description:
The wag who named this terminus of the Sea of Gearnat and made it stick is lost to history, but the appellation is not inappropriate. 

This western part of the Sea of Gearnat is relatively shallow waters, which merchants have sailed for centuries, even before the Great Kingdom …

items.Name: Ulek, County of
items.Description: The mid-most of the three Ulek States, the county is seperated from the duchy to the north by the Kewl River, while the Old River to the south forms the border with the principality. The eastern limit of the county is marked by the Handmaiden River, beginning several leagues no…

items.Name: History: Ulek, County of
items.Description: The County of Ulek has had a long history as one of the more peaceful lands in the Flanaess. The native Flan and halfling peoples were willing to accept Oeridian sovereignty in exchange for protection from the more rapacious Suel, then showed an equal willingness to accept Sulo…

items.Name: Ulek, Duchy of
items.Description: The duchy is one of the three Ulek states, former subjects of the Keoish throne, which still maintains friendly relations with its immediate neighbors. As one of the few countries in the Flanaess ruled by an elf sovereign, the Duchy of Ulek also manages to preserve a harmony be…

items.Name: History: Ulek, Duchy of
items.Description: The Uleks have provided shelter to Good aligned demi-humans for untold centuries, while wars and displaced human nations have moved  across the Flanaess, consuming most of the habitable lands. In the lands of the duchy, elves are the predominant race, though immigrant Suel brie…

items.Name: Ulek, Principality of
items.Description: The Principality of Ulek is the southern most of the three independent Ulek States. It is likely the largest mixed dwarven and human realm in the Flanaess, and one of few that is both possessed and administered by the dwur themselves. The principality sits in the western Flanea…

items.Name: History: Ulek, Principality of
items.Description: Dwarves have lived in these hills since well before the Great Migrations a millenium ago. Treated as an extension of the legendary dwarven kingdoms of the Lortmils at their height, there has been a dwur prince in these foothills long before there was a human king in Niole Dra. …

items.Name: Mountain Ranges: Drachensgrab (Mountains)
items.Description: The small Drachensgrab mounts are highlighted by several towering peaks which thrust up from their center. The whole area is known to be filled with prized metals and fine quality gemstones, but many strange creatures of hostile nature live amidst the hills and mountains of the…

items.Name: Rivers: Jewel River
items.Description: A river which rises just south of the Kron Hills and flows south through the Gnarley Forest, Welkwood, and Suss Forest to empty into the Azure Sea. It divides the Principality of Ulek from the Pomarj. About 150 miles of the waterway are navigable by large craft.

items.Name: Timberlands: Suss Forest
items.Description: The Suss is a dreary place, full of thorn trees, brambles, briars, and thickets. Its massive trees are black with age, and seems to whisper and talk amongst themselves when an interloper dares to pass beneath. Some claim that ripples of waving leaves and moving branches can be …

items.Name: Wastelands: Bright Desert
items.Description: Since the beginning of recorded history in the Flanaess, the Bright Desert has intrigued and challenged mankind. It is supposedly filled with riches - copper, silver, gold, and gem minerals. The harsh climate, wildly varying temperatures, and hostile inhabitants (Suel peoples) …

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Boccob
items.Description:
BOCCOB
(The Uncaring, Lord of All Magic, Archmage of the Deities)

Boccob (BOK-kob) is known throughout the Flanaess, oversees the maintenance of magic's existence on Oerth, and is interested in the creation of new magic items and spells (he is said to have a copy of every magic…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Ehlonna
items.Description:
EHLONNA
(of the Forests)

Ehlonna (eh-LOHN-nah) is a very old goddess. She combats those who would harm or despoil the forest of its resources and beauty. Shown as either a dark-haired human woman or a golden-haired elf maid (in which form she is known to many as Ehlenestra), sh…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Fharlanghn
items.Description:
FHARLANGHN
(The Dweller on the Horizon)

Fharlanghn (far-LAHNG-un) is shown as a seemingly old man with leathery, wrinkled skin and young-seeming bright green eyes. Brother of the Oeridian god Celestian, he is on amiable terms with non-evil earth gods and several nature gods, an…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Heironeous
items.Description:
HEIRONEOUS
(The Invincible, the Valorous Knight, the Arch-paladin)

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Hextor
items.Description:
HEXTOR
(Scourge of Battle, Champion of Evil, Herald of Hell)

Hextor (HEKS-tor) is the arch-foe of Heironeous, his half-brother and fellow Oeridian war god. He seeks to conquer and destroy any that oppose him. He is depicted as a handsome man with dark hair and light skin when s…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Iuz
items.Description:
IUZ
(The Evil, the Old One)

Iuz (EYE-ooze) is thought to be the half-fiend son of the demon lord Graz'zt and the powerful wizard Iggwilv. Appearing on Oerth as a shriveled old man or as a huge, demonic-looking being, Iuz has many fiendish allies and impersonates other gods to f…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Kord
items.Description:
KORD
(The Brawler)

Kord (KOHRD) is an incredibly powerful Suel god, second only to his grandfather, Lendor. Son of Phaulkon and Syrul, he is shown as a hugely muscular man with long red hair and beard, wearing dragonhide gauntlets (white), boots (blue), and fighting girdle (red…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Olidammara
items.Description:
OLIDAMMARA
(The Laughing Rogue)

Olidammara (oh-lih-dam-MAH-rah) loves upsetting those who are too attached to their boring and controlled worlds. He is shown as a brown-haired man of rakish appearance, olive skin, and merry eyes, although his magic laughing mask (and holy symbo…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Pelor
items.Description:
PELOR
(The Sun Father, the Shining One)

Pelor (PAY-lor) is the Flan sun god, known throughout the entire Flanaess. Riding the great ki-rin "Star Thought", he summons flights of eagles and destroys evils with bolts of sunlight. Depicted as an old man in white, with wild hair and…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Pholtus
items.Description:
PHOLTUS
(of the Blinding Light)

Pholtus (FOHL-tus) is a stern Oeridian guardian of unbending Law, depicted as a tall, slender man in a white robe, with fair skin and hair, and eyes that shine with the fires of devotion. He carries the Staff of the Silvery Sun, an ivory object s…

items.Name: Deities of Greyhawk: Saint Cuthbert
items.Description:
SAINT CUTHBERT
(of the Cudgel)

St. Cuthbert (CUTH-bert) may have once been a mortal man as his worshippers claim, but if so it was long ago and from an unknown people. His three prominent symbols are a starburst of rubies, a wooden billet, or a crumpled hat, and while he takes …

items.Description:
